factors.what: US two-year Treasury yield rose about 35 bps this week, the most in over two years, on hot inflation and Fed officials backing a December hike.
factors.channel: Higher US yields and a firmer dollar raise the cost of capital and can weigh on emerging-market equity appetite.

factors.what: Wall Street ended lower, led by tech after an Nvidia-led selloff, and the US 10-year yield moved back above 5%.
factors.channel: Weak global tech sentiment and high US yields can spill into Indian IT and risk appetite, though analysts see limited direct impact.

factors.what: Brent is near $95 a barrel, well below its $118 peak on Oct 30, and the IEA sees the oil market returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover.
factors.channel: Lower crude eases India's import bill and input costs, though prices remain elevated and sensitive to Gulf disruptions.

factors.what: The US-Israel war with Iran has no settlement yet, with renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and strikes on tankers leaving the Gulf.
factors.channel: Supply-disruption risk keeps crude and shipping costs volatile, which feeds India's inflation and external balance.

factors.what: The RBI raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.5% in October, shifted to a 'calibrated tightening' stance, and said near-term cuts are off the table.
factors.channel: A tighter rate path lifts funding costs and bond yields, which weighs on rate-sensitive sectors such as autos, realty and NBFCs.

factors.what: CPI inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance band, with food inflation at 8.94%.
factors.channel: Inflation above the band raises the odds of further RBI tightening, with markets pricing hikes in December and February.

factors.what: The rupee has recovered from about 97 to about 94 per dollar, helped by softer crude and renewed foreign inflows.
factors.channel: A steadier rupee and foreign buying ease imported-inflation and external-funding worries, though rising yields could cap the gains.

factors.what: Q2 results are mixed: Tata Power's profit rose 33%, while Park Medi World's fell 31% on margin pressure.
factors.channel: Stock-specific earnings surprises are driving sector-level moves during the results season.

road_ahead.story: Gulf peace talks progress and crude eases further, which would cool inflation worries and relieve pressure on yields.
signals: Food prices easing in the next CPI print

road_ahead.story: Crude stays in a volatile range and inflation stays above the band, so markets trade on rate expectations and earnings.
signals: RBI December policy tone and vote

road_ahead.story: Talks stall or Gulf attacks escalate, crude and US yields climb, and RBI and Fed tightening expectations rise further.
signals: Further tanker or Saudi infrastructure attacks
Hotter-than-expected US or Indian inflation data

lenses.title: Through a Warren Buffett-style lens
lenses.label: Not their words or views. An AI interpretation of principles they have stated publicly.
lenses.reason: The brief is mostly rates, oil and war headlines, which an owner mindset treats as noise. Higher yields do raise the bar for what counts as a sensible price, so price discipline matters more.
watch: Durable earnings power and pricing power while inflation runs above the RBI band
Low debt on balance sheets as funding costs rise
Gap between price paid and value received as yields climb
avoid: Reacting to one week of market moves
Heavy borrowing
Calls on oil or war outcomes outside the circle of competence

agree: Most lenses put price discipline, balance-sheet strength and avoiding short-term noise ahead of macro calls, with higher yields and inflation raising the bar for valuations.
disagree: The macro-focused lenses (Marks, Dalio, Graham) read rates, inflation and war as a reason for caution, while the business-focused lenses (Kedia, Agrawal, Jhunjhunwala) look through them to management quality and the long-term India growth story.
